title: feat(storage,mcp): an upload link for a file field of a record not yet created
body:
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoSLDKWQ8v7cxY9uDGijfncD)_ Fixes #32686 Clause-②: yes (widening) — nothing narrowed: `create_upload_link` accepts `objectName` + `field` with no `recordId` (where the storage service serves it) and answers `fileIds`; a file id from such a link is accepted in that field on `create_record` / `update_record` by the user who uploaded it, in one record, within an hour of the upload, while no record has held it (once a record has held and released it, it is an ordinary released file). Every existing call answers as before; the only new refusals fall on the new class of file. Metadata-protocol: none — no metadata author key is added, removed or retyped; the binding rides `sys_file.metadata`, the storage row column the upload link's own state already uses. Skills-docs: updated here — the served agent skill (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) teaches the two-call flow where the host serves it; `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` § Files gains the paragraph, and `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` rows 47e/47f name the new caller-scoped verb and the one file a system write can no longer claim (claim amendment 6856718179). The Console's skill mirror renders no file tools, so it is unchanged (its parity test is green). ## 维护者速读 - 改了什么：上传链接可以只指定对象和文件字段、不指定记录。用户用链接上传后，智能体再调用 `create_record`，把链接返回的 `fileIds[0]` 填进该字段，必填文件字段的记录就能建出来（报销明细 + 必填电子发票：两次智能体调用 + 一次浏览器上传）。`required` 规则不变。 - 为什么改：以前链接必须先有记录，而记录又必须先有文件，智能体建不出带必填文件字段的记录。 - 权限与边界：签发时要求该用户能创建该对象的记录、能写该字段、字段不是只读；仍是登录用户、单人、10 分钟过期、一次性（#30892 裁决 B）。上传后的文件只绑定给上传者、该对象该字段、一条记录、一小时内；别人的写入、系统写入、别的字段或对象、第二条记录、超时都会在字段上被拒并说明原因；在被记录占用之前只有上传者能下载。 - 风险与回滚：只放宽（新增调用形态），已有调用和已有文件的判法不变；回滚即 revert。上传后从未被任何记录引用的文件目前不会被回收（与控制台上传后放弃保存同类），已作为范围外发现交席位立卡。 - 先看：`packages/services/service-storage/src/pre-record-upload.ts`（绑定与判定）、`record-file-access.ts` 的 `createUploadLinkForNewRecordAs` 与 `fileForNewRecordThroughLink`、`file-reference-lifecycle.ts` 的 `applyCopyOnClaim` 新分支；验收在 `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts` 末尾的新 describe。 - 需要你做的：无，席位落地。 ## Ruling Maintainer ruling **A** on #32686, recorded by triage 6844207600: 「以上原则同意」 (decision batch #1, `32686 A`): > An upload link can be issued before the record exists (naming the table and field). The user uploads, then the agent creates the record referencing the file id. The `required` rule is unchanged for agents and people. The #30892 ruling B constraint still holds: a signed-in user, one user, expiring. Designed together with #32747 (A); this card goes first and implements one file per link (see "How #32747 adds to this"). ## What changes **Minting a link that names no record** (`RecordFileAccess.createUploadLinkForNewRecordAs`, `record-file-access.ts`). The caller must be a signed-in user (the system context is refused, as for every caller-scoped record-file verb), the field must be a file or image field of the object, and three permission answers must hold for that user: 1. the object's **create** verdict, `security.explain({ object, operation: 'create' }, caller)` — the verdict `create_record`'s own door asks — else `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` "You cannot upload a file for a new X: you cannot create X records."; 2. the field is among `security.getWritableFields(object, caller)`, else `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`; 3. the field is not `readonly`, else `403 FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. This is stricter than the Console form, whose upload (`presign` → `PUT` → `complete`) needs only a session and whose save is judged afterwards; here the save is still judged in full (the create runs under the user's permissions and validations), and the link is refused up front when the save could not succeed on permissions alone. An attachments link still needs its record. A kernel with no security service enforces no object permission on the create either, so there is nothing to ask there. The link is the same single-use, ten-minute, one-user `sys_file` row as a record link (#30892 ruling B), with no `record_id` in its state. Its row id is the file id the upload will be stored under, so the mint can answer it: `fileIds: [id]`. **The upload** (`consumeUploadLink` → `fileForNewRecordThroughLink`). The field's own `accept` and `maxSize` are judged when the file arrives and **before the link is spent** (no record write judges them yet); a file the field cannot take is refused `400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT`, nothing stored, and the link still works. Then the link is spent as before, the bytes are stored, and the reserved row becomes the committed file, owned by the uploader, with a binding in `sys_file.metadata`: ```json { "kind": "pre_record_upload", "object": "expense_line", "field": "invoice", "user_id": "…", "organization_id": "…", "claim_until": "" } ``` The `PUT` answers `{ fileId, size, field }`; the page says the file was received and to go back to the assistant (new `received` copy in all eleven page locales), not that it was attached. **Which write may take the file** (`pre-record-upload.ts#preRecordReferenceRefusal`, asked from `applyCopyOnClaim` in `file-reference-lifecycle.ts` after the read check, before anything is copied or claimed): | The write | While no record holds it | Once a record holds it, within the hour | After the hour | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | the uploader, into the bound object + field | taken | refused (one record) | refused (expired) while no record holds it | | the uploader, another field or object | refused, naming the field it was uploaded for | refused (one record) | refused, naming the field | | another user | refused, in the words of a file they cannot open | refused, same words | refused, same words, while no record holds it | | a system or context-less write | refused, same words | copied, as any record's file | refused while no record holds it | | the record that holds it, rewriting its own value | — | taken (claims nothing) | taken | Once the hour has passed and a record holds the file, it is that record's file like any other: no row above applies, and the read check and copy-on-claim judge it. Every refusal is the ADR-0114 field refusal (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `fields[]` entry `invalid_value` on the field) and refuses the whole write. Another writer gets the existing words for a file they cannot open, so the answer says nothing about whose upload it is; the uploader's own refusals say why (the field it was uploaded for, already in another record, or no record took it within 60 minutes) and end "Ask for a new upload link for this field and upload the file again." A damaged binding (the kind present, a value missing) reads as bound to nobody, so it refuses rather than reading as an ordinary file. **Downloads** (`judgeFileRead`, `storage-service-plugin.ts`). For this new class only — a bound file no record holds, and the pending row its link reserved — only the uploader may download it (the owner arm, unchanged, answers them); everyone else is denied. Once a record holds it, it is that record's file and the existing rules judge it. Every other file is judged exactly as before. **MCP** (`create_upload_link`, `mcp-http-tools.ts`). Where the bridge carries `createUploadLinkForNewRecord`, `recordId` is optional in the listed schema, the description says how, and a call with `field` and no `recordId` answers `{ url, expiresAt, singleUse, objectName, field, fileIds, instructions }`. With no record, `attachments: true` is refused before the bridge is asked. A bridge without the member keeps `recordId` required. The served SKILL.md teaches the flow only where the host says the bridge serves it (`newRecordUploadLinks`, `data:write`). **Runtime** (`domains/mcp.ts`). `McpRecordFileService.createUploadLinkForNewRecordAs?` (optional: a storage plugin that predates it serves record links only); the bridge member answers the link as an absolute URL on the request's origin with its `fileIds`, and reads no record first (there is none; the storage service asks the create verdict). The skill route passes `newRecordUploadLinks`. **No new error code.** Refusals reuse `PERMISSION_DENIED`, `FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `VALIDATION_FAILED` and `ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT`. ## How #32747 adds to this The answer already carries `fileIds` as an array, and the skill already says "the array, for a multi-file field". #32747 adds one optional input (a file count, or `multiple: true` on a multi-file field) and nothing else: the mint reserves one row per file and answers one id per file in the same `fileIds`; the `PUT` door accepts up to that many files; each stored file carries the binding above, unchanged; the create names the array. No key is renamed or retyped and no existing call changes, so it is purely additive. ## Orphans: what reclaims a file uploaded and never referenced - A link never used is its `pending` row, which `sys_file`'s lifecycle `retention` (7 days, `status: 'pending'`) already reaps. - A file uploaded and never put in a record is a committed row with no holder. Nothing reclaims it: the lifecycle reaps only `deleted_at` (30 days) and `pending` rows, the same as for a file uploaded through the Console form and never saved (`stranded-orphan-inventory.ts` calls these rows immortal). After its hour the binding makes it usable by no write, so it is inert, but its bytes stay. Reported to the seat as an out-of-scope finding for a card of its own; not fixed here (ADR-0057 §3.3: no bespoke sweeper). ## Tests - `packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.integration.test.ts`, new describe "#32686 — a link that names no record" (13 cases over a real ObjectQL kernel and the storage routes): the measured case (an `expense_line` with a required `invoice` is refused without it; mint; the create before the upload is refused as never completed; upload; the create naming the id is taken and the file is claimed; the spent link answers 404); the page says "received"; another user refused (unreadable words, file stays unclaimed); a system write refused; another field and another object refused naming the bound field; one record (a second record refused, the first keeps it, the holder's own rewrite admitted); expiry; the update path; downloads (uploader 200, another reader 403, then 200 through the record once claimed); **control**: a Console-style upload (`presign` → raw `PUT` → `complete`) and save is taken as before and carries no binding; minting refusals (system context, non-file field, read-only field, no field); the create verdict and field writability as a security service answers them; `maxSize` refused on arrival with the link not spent. - `packages/services/service-storage/src/pre-record-upload.test.ts` (new, 13 cases): the rule arm by arm, including the other-user arm alone (the integration pin is guarded twice, see the ablations), a damaged binding, a file with no binding, and which rows are uploader-only. - `packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`, new describe (7 cases): the no-record call, a call with `recordId` still asking the record link, attachments with no record refused unasked, the minting refusal relayed with its code, the listed schema (`recordId` optional only where served), a bridge without the member refusing, and the skill paragraph's placement. - `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-file-bridge.test.ts` (2 cases): the member's absolute URL and `fileIds`, no record read; no member without the service verb. - **Acceptance** — `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts`, new describe over a real showcase boot with the security, storage and MCP plugins (3 cases): `create_record` without the e-invoice is refused; **agent call 1** `create_upload_link { objectName: 'dogfood_expense_line', field: 'invoice' }` over `POST /api/v1/mcp`; **the browser** opens the link page (200, "received", names nothing) and uploads through `PUT /api/v1/storage/upload-links/:token`; **agent call 2** `create_record { …, invoice: fileIds[0] }` is taken, the record holds the file, `sys_file` names the record, and `read_file` reads the PDF's text back. Then another signed-in user's create naming a member's upload is refused and cannot download it, while the member's create takes it; and a member who cannot create `showcase_task` gets no link (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`) and nothing is reserved.
Ablations (each committed first, mutated through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs in WRAP mode, restored to the HEAD blob) Every mutation landed (anchor 1 → 0, blob changed) and every restore read `blob == HEAD and git diff HEAD is empty`; `git status` after each set showed no file an ablation touched. ## Acceptance notes - **Measured at `origin/main` `2c98485d`** (order step 1): a create without the required file is refused at the field (the integration measured case asserts it, and `required` is untouched); `create_upload_link` lists `recordId` as required, so a call without it is refused by the schema (ablation 19 reproduces that reading over the real `/api/v1/mcp`); a link for an existing record works (every #30892 pin in the same files is unchanged and green). - **Ruling-surface grep** (`ruling|Ruling-ref|maintainer|⛔`) at the base over the edited files: `file-reference-lifecycle.ts` 2 (organization threading and `actingOrganizationOf`, neither touched), `upload-link-copy.ts` 2 (ruling C on #32440 for page copy, and "⛔ none of them names the record, the object or the field": the new `received` sentence names none), `storage-service-plugin.ts` 18 (none in `judgeFileRead`, where the new arm sits), `mcp-http-tools.ts` 39 (none in `registerFileTools`), `skill-md.ts` 1, `file-content.ts` 1, `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 17 (none in the skill route's file-tools lines or `recordFileMembers`), `record-file-access.ts`, `upload-link-page.ts`, `upload-link-wire.ts`, `file-attachment-service.ts` 0. No ruling sits on an edited line. - **Same-user race.** Two concurrent writes by the uploader naming the same unheld id can both pass the before-write check; the claim never steals, so one record ends up holding the file. This is the existing behaviour for every unclaimed file and stays within one user. - **Typecheck heap.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run typecheck` and `@objectstack/dogfood`'s ran out of heap at Node's default here while other gates ran; both exit 0 with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`. - **Serial.** `domain:server#5` card #32442 edits `mcp-http-tools.ts` near `create_record`, `stdio-data-bridge.ts` and `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`; this seat's #32872 edits the `validate_expression` handler and `skill-md.ts`. This PR touches `registerFileTools`' `create_upload_link` block, `renderFileToolLines` and the new-record skill paragraph, the skill route's three lines, and `McpRecordFileService` / `recordFileMembers`. Whichever lands first, the other merges main once and reruns the affected gates. - **Stdio.** The stdio bridge carries no file members, so the no-record form is HTTP-only, as both file tools are today. ## Verification Readings at head `a9a6589d` (after merging `origin/main` `7c36f524`, which touched none of this PR's files; the four `typecheck` runs and the gates were taken at `0678c15b`, the same tree for these packages), every heavy command under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (VERDICT command-exit 0 on each), exit codes captured before any pipe: - Build: `pnpm turbo run build --concurrency=2 --filter='@objectstack/dogfood^...'` after the merge, 70/70 tasks. - `@objectstack/service-storage` test (whole package): Test Files 82 passed (82), Tests 1540 passed. `typecheck` exit 0. - `@objectstack/mcp` test (whole package): Test Files 63 passed (63), Tests 1104 passed. `typecheck` exit 0. - `@objectstack/runtime` `src/mcp-record-file-bridge.test.ts`: 7 passed. `typecheck` exit 0 (with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, see the notes). - `@objectstack/dogfood` `test/showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts`: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 18 passed (15 existing + 3 new). `typecheck` exit 0 (same heap note). - Lint: `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 17 changed TypeScript files exit 0; the server lane's whole-tree `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) exit 0 at `a9a6589d`. - Derived gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` → 106 families at the final diff (83 before the docs pages joined, 27 more after, plus the four roster gates that keep a roster under one of these paths: `check:changeset-fixed`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:route-ledger-census`, all exit 0), each run with `
